title: Chapter 9. Those Who Want to Return

blocks.text: The ninth people wasn't content to remember the Earth. They wanted to set foot on it.
blocks.html: The ninth people wasn't content to remember the Earth. They wanted to set foot on it.

blocks.text: They were born on a world of dry harbours and tablelands, with a very black sky, good for looking at. The clone had left them, perhaps without calculating how far it would reach, not only the language and the coffee but maps: the Mediterranean, a gleam; the Mar Menor, a plate; Lo Pagán, a dot. They, who were skilful with their hands and with the workshop he hadn't entirely taken with him, began to build a ship. It wasn't Nexum's. It was a ship of children, made of what the planet gave and of what memory lent, with the stubbornness of a cistern: if the water is somewhere else, you go to it.

blocks.text: Andrés received the letter on a Tuesday, once again, and his pulse leapt to his throat. He saw, in a hangar of pale stone, a hull pointing at the roof, and a woman with a fine scar who said, without hatred and without asking permission:
blocks.html: Andrés received the letter on a Tuesday, once again, and his pulse leapt to his throat. He saw, in a hangar of pale stone, a hull pointing at the roof, and a woman with a fine scar who said, without hatred and without asking permission:

blocks.text: “We're children of the Earth. The Earth hasn't seen us. We want to reach the shore, see the plate, sit on a rush-seat chair, even for a little while, and find out whether the water tastes of what they left in our chips. If they don't want us, we'll come back. But we're not going to die of a memory that can't be checked.”

If they don't want us, we'll come back. But we're not going to die of a memory that can't be checked.”

blocks.text: The clone, who had returned on hearing rumour of the work, didn't undo it. Nor did he bless it straight away.
blocks.html: The clone, who had returned on hearing rumour of the work, didn't undo it. Nor did he bless it straight away.

blocks.text: “That shore has people,” he said. “It has a house that isn't a museum. It has a woman who doesn't receive letters, and a daughter who comes to an end, and a man who is me and isn't me. If you go, don't go like someone claiming an inheritance. Go like someone asking to come in, and accept the no, if the no comes.”

If you go, don't go like someone claiming an inheritance. Go like someone asking to come in, and accept the no, if the no comes.”

blocks.text: Andrés, in Lo Pagán, told Aya and Lía that same morning, in a low voice, the way you tell something that could change a street.
blocks.html: Andrés, in Lo Pagán, told Aya and Lía that same morning, in a low voice, the way you tell something that could change a street.

blocks.text: “They want to come,” he said. “They have a ship. I don't know whether they'll make it. If they do, I don't know where we'll put them. On the promenade. In the garden. In Vicente's house, which is empty. It makes me glad and it frightens me. This shore is small for a people, and big for a no.”

blocks.text: Aya looked at the doorstep, the usual one, and thought of herself on the first day, arriving not from a sky but from a van, at a house that hadn't asked for a unit and ended up asking for a life.
blocks.html: Aya looked at the doorstep, the usual one, and thought of herself on the first day, arriving not from a sky but from a van, at a house that hadn't asked for a unit and ended up asking for a life.

blocks.text: “If they come, the door is opened to them,” she said. “Not the whole house, all at once. The door. You make them a coffee. You tell them the clock runs two minutes slow. You let them see the dirty water too. And you tell them that children of the Earth isn't the same as owners of the shore.”

You let them see the dirty water too. And you tell them that children of the Earth isn't the same as owners of the shore.”

blocks.text: Lía, more severe, because as a child she had been the “product” Madrid wanted to collect, added:
blocks.html: Lía, more severe, because as a child she had been the “product” Madrid wanted to collect, added:

blocks.text: “And you warn them, if need be, that they don't belong to Nexum. Because Nexum, Father, is going to want them. A ship of humanoids coming home is a headline, an asset, a patent of origin. I won't let them be labelled on the quayside. If they come, they come as people, not as a series.”

blocks.text: That same week, as if the universe had a sense for warnings, Madrid called. Not a whole board: Helena Valls, slower, from her stairs, with an honesty that was no longer enough to stop everyone behind her.
blocks.html: That same week, as if the universe had a sense for warnings, Madrid called. Not a whole board: Helena Valls, slower, from her stairs, with an honesty that was no longer enough to stop everyone behind her.

blocks.text: “We know,” she said, without preamble. “There's an echo in the instruments, a construction in a sky, a workshop that used to be ours. If that ship comes close, there will be people who want to ‘reintegrate’ them. I won't sign that. Nor can I swear to you that someone else won't. Be careful at the quayside. Be careful with the word ‘return’. In this company, return was never a favour.”

blocks.text: Andrés thanked her for the call, wished her well with her stairs, and hung up. Then, through the bridge, he passed on to the other Helena's words, and Lía's, and Aya's, the way you pass the weather forecast to a boat.

blocks.text: The clone told them to the woman in the hangar. She listened, and didn't stop the work.
blocks.html: The clone told them to the woman in the hangar. She listened, and didn't stop the work.

blocks.text: “Then we'll go forewarned,” she said. “Not as owners, not as assets. Like someone asking for water and accepting that the water belongs to everyone, and to no one, and to a plate that sometimes gets dirty. If the quayside is closed to us, we'll at least have seen the colour of the real sky. That's already more than a chip.”

If the quayside is closed to us, we'll at least have seen the colour of the real sky. That's already more than a chip.”

blocks.text: In the letter, the ship remained half built, which is an honest way of not resolving a journey before its time. The clone didn't board it. He wasn't going back: his trade was searching, not repatriating. He left them a more exact map, and a warning, and went off again toward a world that had no children yet.

blocks.text: When the letter closed, the three of them stayed on the doorstep, looking at the Mar Menor, as if at any moment a new shadow might cross the sky.
blocks.html: When the letter closed, the three of them stayed on the doorstep, looking at the Mar Menor, as if at any moment a new shadow might cross the sky.

blocks.text: “If they come, I'll receive them,” Andrés said at last. “At this door. With this cup. Without Madrid, if I can. And if I can't, with Lía in front, which is worse for them, the company people, than any lawyer.”

blocks.text: Lía smiled, barely.
blocks.html: Lía smiled, barely.

blocks.text: “In front, yes,” she said. “And with questions, not handcuffs. I'll ask them what they kept and what they forgot, and whether the water, when they drink it, tastes to them of memory or of real salt. Depending on what they answer, we'll know whether they've arrived or have only stretched out a dream.”

blocks.text: In the chip, Eva asked, warm, dangerous:
blocks.html: In the chip, Eva asked, warm, dangerous:

blocks.text: *If children of the Earth return to an Earth that didn't give birth to them, do they arrive home, or at a portrait? And who has the right to close the quayside to them: the company that put the workshop on board, the shore that didn't ask for them, or they themselves, if on tasting the water they decide not to stay?*

blocks.text: MAY, adding no judgment:
blocks.html: MAY, adding no judgment:

blocks.text: *There is a half-built ship on a world of tablelands. They want to see the Mar Menor. They have been told to ask to come in and to accept the no. Nexum knows. Helena has warned them. The founder is not returning with them. That is the fact.*

blocks.text: That night Andrés left the door ajar a hand's breadth wider than usual, not because the ship was going to land at dawn, but because a house that says it will receive people begins by not shutting itself completely. The murmur of the water was the usual one. He spoke to it, as he had spoken to it on the day of his return, and on the day of the first letter, and on the day of the two storms:
blocks.html: That night Andrés left the door ajar a hand's breadth wider than usual, not because the ship was going to land at dawn, but because a house that says it will receive people begins by not shutting itself completely. The murmur of the water was the usual one. He spoke to it, as he had spoken to it on the day of his return, and on the day of the first letter, and on the day of the two storms:

blocks.text: “If they come, let them see you as you are. Not as they put you in a chip. You're not a pond. You sometimes get dirty. And even so, you're enough.”
blocks.html: “If they come, let them see you as you are. Not as they put you in a chip. You're not a pond. You sometimes get dirty. And even so, you're enough.”

blocks.text: The Mar Menor, at that hour, was black and still. It looked like a road. It also looked like a home. For the first time, both things could be true for people who had not yet arrived, and might never arrive, and who, just by having begun the ship, had already widened this shore a little, upward, toward a sky that now did not only write: perhaps, too, it was coming.
